blocks.text: This group is often called the Prayer Warriors, or the Power House - a name that reflects the weight of their obligation. While every Christian is called to pray, this group carries a specific responsibility: to pray for the church and to "lift up the hands of Moses" - Moses, in this case, being the Pastor-in-Charge at each level of the church's administration.

items: Voluntarily and personally waiting on God with self-denial - including fasting - to seek His face.
Standing in the gap for individual members facing challenges.
Anchoring prayer sessions before and during services and special programmes, such as "Let's Go A-Fishing."
Providing regular reports of the department's activities to the Pastorate.
Ensuring the spiritual fire on the altar doesn't recede.
A genuine passion for prayer, rooted in love for the church.
Availability - the time to join others at agreed prayer periods.
Holy and righteous living - for protection, since the group stands directly against spiritual opposition on behalf of others.
A love for privacy - willing to work behind the scenes, often withdrawing to an isolated place during big events to avoid distraction and stay focused.
Fearlessness and a dogged, persistent spirit - prayer is warfare, and this calling isn't for those who give up easily.
